subject: anatomy
title: Deep Palmar Spaces, Pulp Infections and Lumbrical Anatomy

steps.tx: Deep to the long flexor tendons and palmar aponeurosis lie two potential fascial compartments bounded by fibrous septa: the thenar space laterally and the **midpalmar space** medially. Separated by an intermediate septum extending from the palmar aponeurosis to the third metacarpal bone, these spaces can harbor deep, closed-space hand infections.
steps.say: Beneath the flexor tendons and palmar aponeurosis lie two potential fascial compartments: the thenar space laterally and the midpalmar space medially. Divided by a fibrous septum anchoring to the third metacarpal, they can harbor deep closed-space infections.

vis.alt: Palmar fascial spaces, thenar space, and midpalmar space boundaries
vis.caption: Deep fascial spaces of the palm and synovial flexor bursa pathways. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The **thenar space** lies anterior to the fascia of adductor pollicis, bounded medially by the intermediate palmar septum and laterally by the lateral septum on the first metacarpal. It communicates distally with the first lumbrical canal. Infection produces intense throbbing pain, ballooning of the thenar web space, and forced thumb abduction.
steps.say: The thenar space lies in front of adductor pollicis, bounded by the intermediate septum medially and the first metacarpal laterally. Infection balloons the first web space with throbbing pain, pushing the thumb into fixed abduction.

left.title: Thenar Space Infection
points: Lies anterior to adductor pollicis muscle
Balloons the first interdigital web space
Forces thumb into fixed palmar abduction
Drained via dorsal web space incision

right.title: Midpalmar Space Infection
points: Lies anterior to 3rd, 4th, 5th metacarpals
Obliterates normal concavity of the central palm
Causes marked swelling on dorsum of hand
Drained via transverse palmar incision

steps.tx: The midpalmar space lies anterior to interosseous fascia over the third, fourth, and fifth metacarpals, bounded medially by the hypothenar septum and laterally by the intermediate septum. Infection obliterates the normal **concavity of the palm**, causing bulging of the central palm accompanied by massive compensatory dorsal hand edema due to loose dorsal subcutaneous lymphatic drainage.
steps.say: The midpalmar space lies over the third to fifth metacarpals beneath flexor tendons. Infection erases the normal concave hollow of the palm, producing a bulging palm with dramatic swelling on the dorsum of the hand from loose lymphatic fluid.

steps.tx: The distal volar pulp of each digit is partitioned into multiple closed tight compartments by vertical fibrous septa extending from the dermis to the periosteum of the terminal phalanx. Acute infection of this closed fibrofatty space is designated a **felon** (whitlow), typically caused by a minor thorn puncture inoculating Staphylococcus aureus.
steps.say: The fingertip pulp is divided into closed compartments by vertical fibrous septa bridging skin to the distal phalanx. Acute closed infection of this pulp space is a felon, typically caused by a minor pinprick introducing staphylococci.

vis.alt: Terminal phalanx pulp space, fibrous septa, and digital artery supply
vis.caption: Digital pulp compartmentalization and blood supply to the distal phalanx. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: As purulent pressure surges within the unyielding pulp compartments, tension compresses digital artery branches supplying the distal phalanx, leading rapidly to ischemic osteomyelitis and necrosis of the **distal phalanx**. Crucially, the extreme proximal base of the phalanx is spared because its epiphyseal blood vessel enters proximal to the closed pulp space.
steps.say: As pressure spikes in the closed pulp space, digital capillaries collapse, leading to ischemic necrosis of the distal phalanx. The base of the phalanx is spared because its epiphyseal vessels enter proximal to the closed pulp space.

left.title: Felon (Pulp Space Whitlow)
points: Closed infection of distal volar pulp
Intense throbbing pain, tense erythematous pad
Causes avascular necrosis of distal phalanx diaphysis
Drained via mid-lateral or longitudinal volar incision

right.title: Paronychia
points: Superficial infection of lateral nail fold
Erythema, swelling, and pus around nail bed
Does not compromise distal phalanx blood supply
Drained by elevating eponychial fold

steps.tx: Infection localized to the lateral nail fold is a **paronychia**, presenting with painful erythema and a localized abscess tracking along the eponychium, managed by elevating the nail fold or partial nail plate avulsion. Unlike a felon, a paronychia does not threaten the nutrient blood supply to the distal phalanx.
steps.say: Infection along the lateral nail fold is a paronychia, presenting with redness and pus around the nail border. Treated by elevating the cuticle, it does not jeopardize the arterial supply of the underlying phalanx.

steps.tx: Deep hand kinematics are coordinated by the **lumbrical muscles**, which arise from the four tendons of flexor digitorum profundus. The first and second lumbricals are unipennate and innervated by the median nerve, while the third and fourth lumbricals are bipennate and innervated by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.
steps.say: Intrinsic finger movements are coordinated by lumbrical muscles arising from flexor digitorum profundus tendons. The first two lumbricals are unipennate and supplied by the median nerve, while the medial two are bipennate and supplied by the deep ulnar nerve.

steps.tx: Lumbricals pass anterior to the deep transverse metacarpal ligament to insert into the lateral margins of the dorsal extensor expansions, flexing the metacarpophalangeal joints and extending the interphalangeal joints. The **interosseous muscles** comprise four dorsal (bipennate, abductors, DAB) and three palmar (unipennate, adductors, PAD), all innervated by the deep ulnar nerve.
steps.say: Lumbricals insert into extensor hoods to flex MCP joints and extend fingers. The interossei comprise four dorsal abductors that spread fingers away from the middle finger, and three palmar adductors that bring fingers together, all innervated by the deep ulnar nerve.

left.title: Dorsal Interossei (DAB)
points: Four bipennate muscles in intermetacarpal spaces
Abduct digits 2, 3, and 4 away from middle axis
Middle finger has two dorsal interossei (no palmar)
Innervated by deep branch of ulnar nerve

right.title: Palmar Interossei (PAD)
points: Three unipennate muscles on palmar metacarpals
Adduct digits 2, 4, and 5 toward middle finger
Middle finger possesses zero palmar interossei
Innervated by deep branch of ulnar nerve
